ig_carousel_topic.topic: Bankroll math for people who've never thought about bankroll
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you bet per game?
Most people guess. There's a better way.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: betting a fixed dollar amount regardless of your total bankroll.
$50 per game sounds fine until you hit a rough week and you're down 30% of your roll.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: Flat-unit betting fixes this. You set one unit as 1-2% of your total bankroll. Every bet is one unit unless you have a strong reason to size up, and even then, rarely above 2 units.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: $1,000 bankroll. One unit = $10 (1%). Seven-pick card, all single units. Worst-case 0-7 day costs $70, or 7% of your roll. Recoverable. Not catastrophic.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: The math isn't complicated. The discipline is. A 54% win rate compounds into real profit over 200+ picks only if you're still in the game in week three.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Bankroll basics most bettors skip. One unit, 1-2% of your roll, every bet. The edge is useless if you bust before it shows up.
